what: Old National Bancorp is a Midwestern bank, based in Evansville, Indiana, lending to businesses and households across Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, Wisconsin and Kentucky.
customers: Small and mid-sized businesses and households across the Midwest.
money: commercial and consumer lending funded by deposits
moat: Community bank deposit franchises assembled across the Midwest by merger, which provide low-cost funding that national banks struggle to match in those towns.
risks: Commercial real estate exposure, as with every regional bank
Growth has come largely from mergers, each of which carries integration risk
Deposit costs rise quickly when rates rise
opportunities: 9.7 times earnings with a 26.5% net margin and $980M of free cash flow
Revenue grew from $811M to $2.5B in four years through the First Midwest and Bremer mergers
Analysts see about 21% upside, with 15 covering the stock
watch: Net interest margin and credit quality in the commercial book.
